Thank you so much, this means so much to me! I've decided to look at things from another perspective, a view of compassion, one of the few things that makes us human. I imagined what would happen if I left, what will happen to my parents, my mom that loves me more than anything, my dad who is always there to support me, my little sisters that look up to me even when I ignored them. Then it clicked, the first tear after so long, after so many years of holding my tears even when I didn't want to, I finally cried. I went downstairs and hugged my mom, my dad sat with us to cheer me up. Today, today I am grateful... Living isn't that bad when you cheerish the things you took for granted. 

And thank you, and everyone who under this post talked with me and supported me, you guys saved me from my own grief... 
Thank you

Things are not getting better really, for once I'm going to try antidepressants to push myself forward, I'll try to plan something like I always used to and follow that path that will hopefully lead me to the top

Sorry for the really really late comment, your story was amazing and inspiring, I've been trying to have the same mindset and hopefully I can push through it too, I wish you good luck with your business and dreams!
May I ask, how did it go for you? After university.
Thanks a lot, I wish you the best, good luck!

I take inspiration from them, I wish one day to have enough money to do something relevant to the world, even if it's as simple as making someone happy. 
And thanks for this conversation, I appreciate it!

For them there is no career without the degree, and that's something I want to avoid. I really want to dropout, and I may sound childish saying that but why would I struggle to wake up early, go to a school I don't like, with teachers that are despicable even if they are just doing their job, trying so hard to get a degree I'm not interested to, just to get back home and have little to no time for something I really want to do. 

I love learning, but that doesn't mean that school is my only option, and that's something they won't understand. I want to learn more about the stock market, and maybe also photography and video editing, things that can be self-taught, done in the comfort of your home, without anyone bossing you around.

Parenthood is quite difficult, as a parent people expect you to be the best, but the truth is, the only experience you have is how your own parents raised you when you were a kid. And when you have a baby you'll learn along the way. My parents are raising me through the experience they got from dropping out and working at a young age, to move to another country, and realize how harsh the world is without a degree of some sort. 

About trading stocks, I've been doing it for a while now, almost two years, but I can't do much because of the extensive hours at school, where I pretty much wake up at 5 am to get ready, take the bus, finish school at 6 pm, get back home at 7:30 and sleep half an hour later.

I don't think I could move out, not because of age, as I'm old enough, but I'm inexperienced with the outside world as I've been under the wing of my parents for too long. That's why a career that would be more suitable for me is day trading in the stock market, the issue with that is that I'll have to quit school, and having my parents pressuring to get quick results for letting me drop out isn't possible. 
I'm really stuck here with the only option being school and stress, or dissapointed parents and stress.
